name: VAPEUR-RCT
question: In sexually active men with benign prostatic obstruction refractory to alpha-blocker therapy, is Rezūm water vapor therapy noninferior and then superior to combination pharmacotherapy for urinary symptoms, and superior for sexual-function preservation?

design.population: 151 sexually active men aged at least 45 years with symptomatic benign prostatic obstruction refractory to alpha-blocker monotherapy were randomized; entry required IPSS at least 13, Qmax at most 15 ml/s, PVR at most 250 ml, and prostate volume at least 30 ml.
design.description: Multicenter, pragmatic, open-label randomized trial with gated IPSS noninferiority and superiority tests and an MSHQ superiority test
design.locator: Full text, Methods §§2.1–2.5, p 3; Table 1, p 4

verdictNote: IPSS noninferiority and superiority met; MSHQ superiority failed under multiple imputation.
takeaway: In sexually active men with benign prostatic obstruction refractory to alpha-blocker monotherapy, Rezūm met IPSS noninferiority and superiority versus an alpha-blocker plus a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor at 1 year. MSHQ superiority did not meet its prespecified threshold with multiple imputation.

reports.label: 1-year report
reports.citation: Vincendeau S, Xylinas E, Fourmarier M, et al. "Water Vapor Thermal Therapy with Rezūm Versus Combination Pharmacotherapy for Male Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms due to Benign Prostatic Obstruction: 1-Yr Results From a Prospective, Multicenter, Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial (VAPEUR-RCT)." *Eur Urol Focus.* 2026 Aug 18:S2405-4569(26)00175-6. doi:10.1016/j.euf.2026.08.001
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods §2.4 and Results §3.1, p 3

results.measure: Available-case baseline-to-12-month IPSS change in the randomized cohort; 3-point noninferiority margin
results.note: The negative difference is Rezūm minus combination therapy for change scores; the upper CI bound is below the prespecified +3-point noninferiority margin.
results.locator: Full text, Methods §§2.4–2.5, p 3; Results §3.2, p 4; Abstract, pp 1–2

results.measure: Available-case mean baseline-to-12-month IPSS improvement; difference in change scores, Rezūm minus combination therapy
results.note: The negative mean difference is for change scores; the arm values are improvements. With multiple imputation, the difference was −6.5 points (97.5% CI −9.8 to −3.2; p < 0.0001). At 12 months, IPSS was 0–7 in 33/63 versus 8/57 available cases.
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.5, p 3; Results §3.2, p 4; Figs 1–2, pp 5–6; Abstract, p 1

results.measure: Mean baseline-to-1-year Male Sexual Health Questionnaire score change
results.note: The MICE comparison did not meet the prespecified one-sided 1.25% threshold. LOCF showed a 6.5-point difference (97.5% CI 0.7–12.3; p = 0.006).
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.5, p 3; Results §3.2, p 4

results.measure: Mean baseline-to-12-month IPSS quality-of-life item change
results.note: Lower scores represent improvement; the reported p value was not part of the multiplicity-controlled endpoint hierarchy.
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.5, p 3; Results §3.4, p 4; Fig 1C, p 5

results.note: One photolaser vaporization after Rezūm; four Rezūm procedures, two photolaser vaporizations, and one bipolar transurethral vaporization after combination therapy.
results.locator: Full text, Results §3.3, p 4; Table 2, p 6

results.note: The nine Rezūm patients received six alpha-blocker regimens, two anticholinergics, and one combination regimen.
results.locator: Full text, Results §3.3, p 4; Table 2, p 6

results.measure: Time to surgical treatment, new BPO medication, catheterization after 90 days, or IPSS worsening by at least 4 points through 1 year
results.locator: Full text, Methods §§2.4–2.5, p 3; Results §3.3, p 4

results.measure: IPSS worsening of at least 4 points from baseline through 1 year
results.note: The two Rezūm patients worsened at 3 months but improved below baseline by 6 months.
results.locator: Full text, Results §3.3, p 4; Table 2, p 6

results.measure: Urinary retention requiring catheterization after 90 days post-treatment
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.4, p 3; Results §3.3, p 4; Table 2, p 6

harms.label: Treatment-related adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 7; Results §3.4, p 4
harms.note: There were 50 versus 40 treatment-related events; 44/50 Rezūm events occurred within 90 days.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Results §3.4, p 4; Table 3, p 7
harms.note: Nine versus two serious events affected nine versus one patients; six Rezūm events were procedure-related: urinary retention (2), bacterial prostatitis (1), prostatic obstruction (1), persistent LUTS (1), and anejaculation (1).

harms.label: Infections after Rezūm
harms.note: The report says all infections were Clavien-Dindo grade II; six patients had bacterial prostatitis, including one serious case.

harms.label: Catheterization to manage an adverse event
harms.note: This action-taken category differs from the secondary endpoint of catheterization after 90 days.

values.exp: Ambulatory Rezūm water vapor thermal therapy under general anesthesia within 45 days (permitted up to 90 days) of randomization
values.ctl: Continued alpha-blocker and added a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor within 7 days of randomization

delivery.label: Procedure characteristics

values.exp: 5.1 ± 2.1 vapor treatments per prostate; mean procedure 13.8 ± 16.6 min (n = 72); median lobe treated in 45/72 (63%)

delivery.locator: Full text, Results §3.1, p 3; Table 1, p 4
delivery.note: All Rezūm patients were discharged the same day with a catheter; mean dwell time was 5.8 ± 2.20 days (Methods §2.3, p 3).

delivery.label: Medication adherence

values.ctl: 75% self-reported taking at least 85% of doses at 1 year

delivery.locator: Full text, Methods §2.3 and Results §3.1, p 3
delivery.note: The percentage denominator is not stated in the main text.
